title: SLO-aligned adaptive throttler with transparent accounting
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Production incidents show that during large tenant bursts and partial limiter outages we either over-fail (hard drops) or silently favor high-throughput tenants. Objective: implement an SLO-aligned adaptive throttler that enforces global and tenant quotas while providing transparent accounting (per-tenant consumed tokens and approximation of fairness decisions). The system must operate across multi-region deployments with mode-specific behavior for region-isolated outages: graceful degradation, lease transfer, and probabilistic admission to preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants. Deliverables: a new admission controller service (read-only failover mode), a lightweight telemetry schema for fairness/denial attribution, deterministic simulated workloads for chaos/resilience testing, and a rollout plan with canary toggles and fallbacks to current limiter. This ticket covers design, prototype, canary rollout, and documentation updates for Console visibility and SLO dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive throttler enforces per-tenant and global limits with <5% SLA breach measured on test harness under 2x expected burst workload
Telemetry includes per-request admission outcome, reason code (quota, fairness, circuit), tenant priority, and approximate token accounting

Multi-region failover path: when regional limiter unavailable, requests are (a) probabilistically admitted up to a calculated local buffer, (b) optionally routed to another region per policy, and (c) correctly reconciled in accounting within 2 minutes
Circuit breaker integration triggers degradations (soft deny / reduced rate) rather than hard rejects for tenants with active SLO exemptions
Console surfaces a per-tenant fairness score, recent denied reasons, and suggested remediation for high-deny tenants
End-to-end chaos test demonstrates recovery from simulated limiter outage with less than 10% client error rate and no tenant starvation
tasks: Design: finalize admission algorithm and fairness heuristics (probabilistic admission, token decay, priority weighting)
Implement: admission controller prototype in Go with pluggable scoring function
Implement: telemetry producer (Event schema v2) and add to router and admission points
Testing: extend workload generator to include skewed tenant distributions and long tail bursts
Chaos: author chaos engineering experiments to simulate limiter node crash and network partition
Console: add read-only panel with per-tenant accounting and denial reasons
Docs: PRD and runbook for operator recovery and post-incident steps
Rollout: plan canary and automated rollback, include alerting thresholds and SLO dashboards
decisions: Use probabilistic admission instead of strict FIFO token queues to reduce tail latency under burst
Adopt a lightweight, append-only per-tenant accounting event stream (no global sync in hot path) for performance
Circuit breaker states will prefer soft-deny (503 with Retry-After or partial tokens) for high-priority tenants
Inter-region routing for capacity is opt-in per tenant; default behavior is local probabilistic buffering plus reconciliation
